claims.statement: `create_deep_agent` separates declarative and compiled synchronous subagents from `AsyncSubAgent` specs, adds a default synchronous `general-purpose` worker unless the harness profile disables or replaces it, and installs the synchronous `task` middleware and asynchronous task middleware independently.

A synchronous declarative subagent is isolated by default: it receives a new task message and state with messages, todos, structured response, skill metadata, pinned skills, disclosure metadata, fork marker, and private fields excluded; explicit child permissions or `interrupt_on` replace inherited values, while omitted values inherit the parent configuration.

Experimental `mode="fork"` reconstructs the parent's effective history and prompt context for a delegated task but forbids an independent skills list and refuses nested `task` calls, preventing recursive delegation.

Async subagents launch Agent Protocol runs in remote threads and persist task metadata in `async_tasks`; dedicated tools then check results, replace a running task's run on update, cancel it, or list refreshed status, while URL-less ASGI transport requires an async parent invocation.

`SkillsMiddleware` discovers `SKILL.md` metadata through backend APIs, overlays same-named skills by source order, caches the resulting index in `skills_metadata` until it is set to `None`, and injects a progressive-disclosure prompt that directs the model to read full instructions on demand.

Skill-selected tools are not registered in the ordinary tool node; a successful `read_file` result for a known skill's `SKILL.md` or a pinned-skill message resolves `metadata.include_tools` for a subsequent model call, and records only gated tools in `_skill_tools_disclosed`.

At execution time, `SkillsMiddleware` admits an otherwise unregistered skill tool only when the latest disclosure record maps its name to an include name and the resolver still returns it; unrecorded, same-turn, or stale-resolution calls remain invalid-tool errors.

Async launches attach the parent thread ID to remote thread metadata; same-deployment launches can forward run context or a `deepagents_parent` reference containing parent thread and assistant IDs, whereas cross-deployment launches deliberately omit the assistant ID and retain only the parent thread reference.

A successful remote run whose thread is interrupted is tracked as nonterminal `waiting`; checks return its pending interrupts, an external resume can be recovered by adopting the newest run, and cancellation or update of a waiting task respectively preserves cancellation or replaces the outstanding human request.

Every graph installs `_ParentNotifierMiddleware`; for a top-level Deep Agent child with a parent reference, the async hooks report success or model failure once and attempt to wake only an idle same-deployment parent, while pauses do not notify and delivery failures do not fail the child.

On async invocations, `AsyncSubAgentMiddleware` polls unfinished tasks at agent start, before model calls, and after a final answer; changed success, error, timeout, or waiting outcomes are inserted as marked user messages framed as system notifications, and a post-answer notification sends the model for another turn.

The local `task` boundary rejects unknown model arguments, requires a tool-call ID, and returns either JSON-serialized structured output or the last nonempty child AI text in one correlated `ToolMessage`, filtering excluded, private, and unchanged state updates.

Remote async task records are merge-reduced by task ID and retain task/thread identity, agent and run IDs, cached status, and lifecycle timestamps; list filtering uses cached status before refreshing nonterminal tasks, and SDK refresh failures preserve the cached status.

Pins are consumed before a model call: known distinct skills are read in first-seen order, their frontmatter-free bodies become attributed `HumanMessage` snapshots, and `pinned_skills` is cleared; unavailable or unreadable skills are skipped.

Skill disclosure controls model visibility and tool availability rather than authorization: after a read or pin, the middleware records exactly the gated tools shown to the model, but any disclosed tool remains subject to the ordinary permission and human-in-the-loop middleware stack.

For models that support mid-conversation tools, skill disclosures are anchored after the read's complete tool-result batch using Anthropic `tool_addition` or OpenAI Responses `additional_tools` blocks; unsupported Anthropic root combinator schemas are withheld so the disclosure record matches model-visible definitions.

The self-hosted async-subagent example implements the Agent Protocol thread, run, polling, result-fetch, cancellation, and health endpoints over FastAPI with in-memory SQLite; it is explicitly demonstration-only, without authentication or rate limiting, and its cancellation route records cancellation without cancelling the in-flight agent coroutine.
